correctness.rationale: Kitano--Nakae prove \(\Delta_K\doteq P_T(\Delta_{\hat K})^2\). In the UFD \(\mathbb Z[t,t^{-1}]\), a reciprocal Laurent polynomial is a Fox--Milnor norm exactly when every self-reciprocal irreducible orbit has even multiplicity; multiplication by the reciprocal square \((\Delta_{\hat K})^2\) changes those multiplicities only by even amounts. Thus \(\Delta_K\) is a norm exactly when \(P_T\) is. For a repeated numerator polynomial \(Q\), \(Q^n\) is a norm for even \(n\), while if \(Q\) has any odd self-reciprocal irreducible multiplicity then the same obstruction remains for odd \(n\). The polynomial \(2t^2-3t+2\) is self-reciprocal and irreducible because its discriminant is \(-7\), so the advertised odd-copy obstruction is correct.

final_claim: For a Kitano--Nakae multiple-tangle extended symmetric union \(K\), the Fox--Milnor norm status of \(\Delta_K\) is exactly the norm status of the product of the numerator-knot Alexander polynomials; consequently repeating a fixed non-norm numerator tangle passes the Fox--Milnor test exactly for an even number of copies, while the displayed \(5_2\) numerator obstructs sliceness for every odd repetition.
limitations: This is only the classical Alexander-polynomial Fox--Milnor obstruction; passing it does not imply sliceness.
The conclusion is specific to the Kitano--Nakae product formula and does not control signatures, Casson--Gordon invariants, Floer invariants, or twisted Alexander polynomials.
